This article compares the characteristics of newly diagnosed adult patients and prevalent (previously diagnosed) adult patients who had a hospital contact for inflammatory bowel disease ([[ibd|IBD]]) and related conditions between October 1, 2023, and September 30, 2024 [^src1]. Because the data represents a single reporting period, no longitudinal trends can be established; the analysis focuses strictly on the cross-sectional differences between the two cohorts [^src1].

In terms of diagnoses, [[colitis-ulcerosa|Colitis ulcerosa]] is the clear leader for both groups, accounting for 58% of newly diagnosed patients (1,275 individuals) and 58% of prevalent patients (17,606 individuals) [^src1]. [[crohns-sygdom|Crohns sygdom]] follows as the second most common condition, representing 41% in both cohorts [^src1]. The rarest conditions, acting as trailers, are [[psc|Primær skleroserende kolangitis (PSC)]] at 1% for both groups, and [[korttarmssyndrom|korttarmssyndrom]] at 0% (9 newly diagnosed and 79 prevalent patients) [^src1].

Demographically, women make up the majority of both cohorts, leading with 51% of newly diagnosed patients and 54% of prevalent patients [^src1]. However, the age distribution reveals a significant outlier pattern between the two groups. For newly diagnosed patients, the 18-29 age group is the dominant leader, comprising 30% (668 individuals) of the cohort [^src1]. In contrast, the prevalent patient population is much more evenly spread across middle and older age brackets, with the 30-39 and 50-59 age groups tying as leaders at 19% each [^src1]. The 90 years or older category is the absolute trailer for both groups, representing 0% of the population [^src1].

Regarding hospital contact types, physical attendance is the leading method of interaction, accounting for 66% of contacts for newly diagnosed patients and 64% for prevalent patients [^src1]. Virtual contacts make up the remaining 34% and 36%, respectively [^src1].

Entities: ibd, crohns-sygdom, colitis-ulcerosa, psc, korttarmssyndrom

Summary: Tabellen sammenligner procentvise karakteristika for nydiagnosticerede og tidligere diagnosticerede voksne med IBD, og viser at colitis ulcerosa dominerer blandt nydiagnosticerede (58 %), at kvinder udgør flertallet blandt voksne (54 %), og at aldersfordelingen er bredest i 30–59-årsgruppen.
